Teufel (1986), hereafter referred to as Warpinski's method, solved the viscoelastic equation in terms of principal strain magnitudes and variable parameters that are related to principal stress magnitudes by means of distortional creep compliance argument. The resultant exponential equa- tions are used as model to extrapolate the measured data to the time the

samples were cut downhole. Values for the variable parameters are derived from the extrapolated curve fit and used to calculate the maximum horizontal stress and creep compliance argument provided the minimum horizontal stress is known.
